title: Postnikov convergence in the pro-étale derived category
statement:
For every complex $K$ of $\mathcal R$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, the map of
complexes

$$
\iota\colon K\to R\varprojlim_n\tau_{\geq-n}K=\operatorname{Cone}\Bigl(\prod_n\tau_{\geq-n}K
\xrightarrow{1-T}\prod_n\tau_{\geq-n}K\Bigr)[-1],\qquad k\mapsto\bigl((\bar k_n)_n,0\bigr),
$$

where $\bar k_n$ is the image of $k$ in $\tau_{\geq-n}K$, is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Naturality of the good lower-truncation quotient and cancellation of its invertible further truncation give pi_(n+1) followed by postnikovStep n = pi_n. Identify the successor map of Functor.ofOpSequence with postnikovStep. After every product projection the quotient-family map followed by 1-T is zero, so the zero-null-homotopy comparison is a chain map.

For each integer q, the quotient induces an isomorphism on H^q when n >= -q, by the good-truncation quasi-isomorphism in retained degrees; below that bound the cohomology is zero. Functoriality gives compatibility with transitions. The transitions on cohomology are therefore epimorphisms. Apply det-pe-milnor-epimorphic to conclude that 1-T on the product of cohomologies is epic.

Use the projection-compatible cohomology/product comparison of det-pe-products-derived, transporting from the coefficient-universe ULift of N to N. Product extensionality and functoriality identify H^q(1-T) under this comparison with 1-T on the cohomology tower. Consequently H^q(1-T) is epic in every degree. Exactness of the mapping-cocone triangle then makes H^q of its first projection monic and identifies it as a kernel.

Prove directly the kernel property of the product of quotient maps on cohomology. At N=max(0,-q), invert the quotient map to recover a map to H^q(K) from any compatible product family. Induction using invertible tail transitions proves the factorization for all n>=N; the zero target gives it for n<N. The Nth component gives uniqueness. Transport this kernel along the cohomology/product comparison. The actual mapping-cocone lift composed with its first projection is the quotient family. Its map on H^q is thus the unique isomorphism between these two kernels. This holds for every q, proving the specified comparison is a quasi-isomorphism.
